title.narrative: Joint Programme to Build and Strengthen Urban Rural Resilience and the Conditions for Recovery in Syria (Phase II) Sustainability Workplan

description.narrative:
The Joint Progamme (Phase II) is a continuity of the the Joint Programme Phase (I) (same outcomes). The JP (Phase I) was implemented by six Agencies (UN-Habitat, UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, FAO and WFP); started in 2019 with an end date on 14 January 2021 and extended until 2023. The JP (Phase I) and (Phase II) have the same outcomes (3 outcomes) and the same outputs with different activities. The HQ PAG meeting minutes were signed and approved in April 2017 with a total budget of USD 70,766,349.
The UN Joint Programme funded by the EU (19,000,000 EUR) and Norway (60,000,000 NOK) and was implemented by six UN Agencies (UN-Habitat, UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, FAO, WFP) technically led by the UN-Habitat Syria Programme from 2017 until 2019. The share of UN-Habitat was US$ 3,821,499. In 2020, the Programme Management Unit (PMU) was established at the UN Resident Coordinator Office and took the leadership of the UN Joint Programme. In 2019-2023, the Participating UN Organizations (PUNOs) implemented a package of integrated activities enhancing the resilience of the population in Dar'a and Deir Ez Zor which is named UNJP phase I. The implementation was divided into two stages in Dara City and one stage in Deir Ez Zor City. In 2022, Italy funded the UN Joint Programme (EURO 2,000,000) to support and enhance the sustainability of the projects that were implemented in Daraa and Deir Ez Zor City. In Nov 2023, JP URR’s Participating UN Organizations signed an agreement with the MPTFO which is the Financial Administrative Agent. Out of the EURO 2M amount, UN-Habitat’s Share is only 335,000 US$. The Joint Programme is still has unfunded budget 40,362,226.5 USD out of the aforementioned USD 70,766,349. Accordingly, the inception phase of the JP URR 2.0 is in progress targeting Aleppo Governorate.
Returning to the UN Joint Programme for Urban and Rural Resilience Phase II (Sustainability Workplan) funded by Italy, it will be implemented by the same six UN Agencies as mentioned earlier. UN-Habitat's activities will contribute to the achievement of the Joint Programme's Outcomes: - Outcome 2 "Basic and social services restored, improved and sustained to enhance community resilience and social cohesion"; And - Outcome 3 "Households and communities benefit from sustainable livelihood opportunities, including economic recovery and enhancing social cohesion and community security". The (JP) during its current phase of implementation supported the resilience of Syrian people through jointly designed, and planned interventions ensuring complementarity and avoiding duplication and overlap, in two targeted locations Dara’a and Deir ez-Zor. It was agreed in the JP’s Joint Steering Committee (JSC) meeting held on 27th October 2022, that the JP in its second phase will ensure that the gains made during its first phase of implementation are sustained and built upon by the local community. This will be done by maintaining and expanding on a group of approved interventions that will further enhance the resilience of people and ensure a smoother exit of the JP from its current locations. The sustainability response plan builds on the approved JP response plans for Dara’a and Deir-ez-Zor, whose interventions have either been completed or progressing toward completion. The sustainability response plan is intended to capitalize on the achievements and gains made through the implementation of key resilience-supporting interventions. The JP identified three key bases on which, the sustainability of interventions depends and consequently will ensure a confident and smooth exit of the JP. A. Community engagement and empowerment: Meaningful engagement with all relevant individuals of diverse ages and backgrounds, with a particular focus on young people, women and girls to ensure they can express their views and participate in decision-making about how to sustain the gains made in phase I. Community’s capacities will be enhanced to sustain access to critical livelihood systems as well as basic services in a manner that enables them to 1) help the most vulnerable families generate sustainable income, 2) enhance the community’s financial capacity to improve access to basic services including reproductive health (RH) services, learning and skills-building opportunities. The JP participating UN organizations (PUNOs) will support the role of neighborhoods and village committees in managing the community’s resources to anticipate and mitigate risks. PUNOs will advocate with different stakeholders to ensure that young people, women and other vulnerable and marginalized groups participate meaningfully in the committees. B. Support to service-provision facilities: the JP PUNOs will perform a light rehabilitation of existing local facilities, C. Improved urban-rural market dynamics and sustained livelihoods.
